column1: # services/gluetun/env.tsv — gluetun's rows of the .env schema (columns: lib/env.schema.tsv)

column7: the VPN provider: a folder of services/gluetun/providers (gluetun's name, spaces as hyphens)
the tunnel the provider is run with (each provider's folder says which it offers; WireGuard where it has both)
the VPN's WireGuard private key
the WireGuard interface address, for a provider that gives one per key (empty: the provider's own, e.g. NordVPN's and ProtonVPN's)
the WireGuard pre-shared key, for a provider that needs one (AirVPN, Windscribe)
the VPN's OpenVPN username — the provider's service login for manual setup, usually not the website's
the VPN's OpenVPN password (the same service login)
OpenVPN over UDP or TCP (TCP: slower, for networks that block UDP; each provider's folder says which it offers)
the OpenVPN client certificate, for a provider that gives one (AirVPN, CyberGhost, VPN Unlimited, VPNSecure): its base64 body, one line
the OpenVPN client key (PKCS#8, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY), for a provider that gives one (AirVPN, CyberGhost, VPN Unlimited): its base64 body, one line
limit the VPN to servers in these regions (comma-separated, as gluetun's server list spells them; empty = any; each provider's folder says what it offers)
limit the VPN to these countries (comma-separated; empty = any)
limit the VPN to these cities (comma-separated; empty = any)
limit the VPN to servers of these hosting ISPs (comma-separated; empty = any; IVPN, Mullvad)
limit the VPN to servers of these categories (comma-separated, e.g. P2P; empty = the provider's own: NordVPN's standard servers; NordVPN, PureVPN)
limit the VPN to servers with all these flags (comma-separated: owned, free, stream, secure-core, tor — each provider's folder says which it has; empty = none)
limit the VPN to these server hostnames (comma-separated; empty = any) — never asked: a hostname gone from gluetun's list stops the tunnel (up refuses it first)
a port forwarded to the download client, so peers can connect in (seeding) — only for a provider that forwards one (each provider's folder says); off changes nothing for downloads
the port your provider's site forwards to you, for one that forwards a port you set (AirVPN, Windscribe); the others arrange their own
gluetun's encrypted DNS resolvers, asked through the tunnel (comma-separated, e.g. cloudflare,quad9)
gluetun no longer reads it; a plaintext DNS server there could send queries outside the tunnel (VPN_DNS_RESOLVERS)
the key every route of gluetun's control server needs — nothing in the stack holds it: the control server is closed, whatever the image's default (generated)
